metadata.description: Azure DevOps service

Kibana dashboards are web interfaces for visualizing Elasticsearch data. If exposed without authentication, they can lead to massive data leaks, including logs, metrics, and potentially sensitive business data.
reproductionSteps: If a Kibana dashboard loads without prompting for a login, the instance is likely misconfigured.
Explore the available dashboards and data indices for sensitive information.

metadata.description: Exposed Zoom recordings/configurations
metadata.impact: Sensitive meeting content and configurations may be leaked, leading to privacy breaches and corporate espionage.
metadata.remediation: Require authentication for accessing recordings, disable public sharing, and enforce company-wide access policies.

metadata.description: Notion pages accidentally exposed publicly
metadata.impact: Confidential company documentation may be publicly accessible and indexed by search engines.
metadata.remediation: Review Notion sharing settings, restrict sensitive pages, and disable public sharing.

metadata.description: Shared Airtable bases with sensitive data exposed
metadata.impact: PII, business data, or API keys may be leaked through public Airtable bases.
metadata.remediation: Set bases to private, enable strict access controls, and avoid sharing sensitive information in Airtable.
metadata.reproduce: Access shared Airtable base link without login.

metadata.description: Public Trello boards indexed by Google
metadata.impact: Exposed boards may contain company roadmaps, employee emails, or project details.
metadata.remediation: Set boards to private, enforce organization-wide board visibility policies.

metadata.description: Shared file links exposed to unauthorized users
metadata.impact: Confidential documents may be leaked if shared links are not properly secured.
metadata.remediation: Disable public file sharing, enable link expiry and password protection, audit existing shared links.
metadata.reproduce: Access a Dropbox/Box link without authentication.

metadata.description: Open Kibana dashboards / Elasticsearch instances
metadata.impact: Attackers may exfiltrate logs, modify dashboards, or even manipulate live data.
metadata.remediation: Restrict access with authentication, firewall rules, and enable TLS encryption.
metadata.reproduce: Visit https://target.com:5601 or https://target.com:9200 without login.

metadata.description: Insecure Firebase database rules
metadata.impact: Attackers may read/write arbitrary data, leading to data theft or modification.
metadata.remediation: Enforce proper Firebase rules, restrict unauthenticated read/write access.

metadata.description: Docker registries storing container images can be misconfigured to allow unauthenticated access, potentially leaking proprietary application code and secrets embedded in images.
reproductionSteps: Visit the URL /v2/_catalog to list available repositories
Use tools like skopeo or docker pull to access images
Analyze images for sensitive data or credentials

metadata.description: Redis instances without authentication can expose sensitive cached data, session stores, and even allow remote code execution through module loading or Lua sandbox escape.
reproductionSteps: Run commands: INFO, KEYS *, CONFIG GET *
Check for sensitive data in keys and values

metadata.description: MongoDB databases without authentication can expose sensitive business data, PII, and potentially allow full database compromise including data exfiltration or destruction.
reproductionSteps: Run commands: show dbs, show collections, db.adminCommand({listDatabases:1})

metadata.description: When .git directories are publicly accessible, attackers can download the entire source code repository, including commit history, configuration files, and potentially sensitive credentials.
reproductionSteps: Use tools like git-dumper or DVCS-Pillage to download repository
Analyze source code and commit history for secrets

metadata.description: The Jenkins Script Console allows execution of arbitrary Groovy code. If accessible without authentication, it can lead to complete system compromise and remote code execution.
reproductionSteps: Execute Groovy code to confirm access
Use for remote code execution and privilege escalation

metadata.description: FTP servers configured for anonymous access can expose sensitive files, backup data, and potentially provide a foothold for further network penetration.
reproductionSteps: List directories and download accessible files

metadata.description: The wp-config.php file contains database credentials, authentication keys, and other sensitive configuration details. Public access can lead to complete site compromise.
reproductionSteps: Extract database credentials and other secrets

metadata.description: etcd is a distributed key-value store used by Kubernetes and other systems. Public access can expose cluster configuration, secrets, and authentication tokens, leading to complete cluster compromise.
.env files contain sensitive environment variables, database credentials, API keys, and application secrets. Public exposure can lead to complete application compromise.
reproductionSteps: Extract credentials and secrets from the file

metadata.description: Misconfigured SMTP servers allowing open relaying can be abused to send spam emails, phishing campaigns, and conduct email spoofing attacks.
reproductionSteps: Connect via telnet or nc: telnet {TARGET} 25
Test for open relay: EHLO test, MAIL FROM:, RCPT TO:
Verify if server accepts external recipient addresses

metadata.description: API endpoints exposed without proper authentication can lead to data leakage, unauthorized access, and potential business logic vulnerabilities.
API documentation exposed publicly can reveal endpoint details, parameters, and potentially sensitive API information that could aid attackers in crafting targeted attacks.
MySQL databases running on default port 3306 and exposed to untrusted networks can be targeted for unauthorized access, especially with weak or default credentials.
reproductionSteps: Connect using mysql client: mysql -h {TARGET} -u root -p
Try empty password or common default credentials (root, admin, test)
Run commands: SHOW DATABASES; SELECT User, Host FROM mysql.user;

metadata.description: PostgreSQL instances allowing public access on port 5432 with weak authentication methods (trust, md5) can lead to full database compromise and data exfiltration.
reproductionSteps: Try trust authentication or empty password
Execute: \l to list databases, \du to list users, SELECT * FROM pg_user;

metadata.description: Microsoft SQL Server instances exposed on default port 1433 can be targeted for brute force attacks, especially if mixed mode authentication is enabled with weak sa passwords.
reproductionSteps: Try common credentials (sa with blank password, admin/admin)
Execute: SELECT name FROM sys.databases; SELECT * FROM sys.sql_logins;

Query time-series hypertables: SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.hypertables;
